cards.headline: The label wanted it as the A-side; the band wasn't sure
cards.snippet: In 1989, the Stone Roses recorded "Fools Gold" and "What the World Is Waiting For" at Sawmills Studios in Cornwall, planning the latter as the A-side. Then Roddy Mckenna, the A&R man at their label Silvertone, heard "Fools Gold" and urged the band to lead with it instead. They weren't fully convinced, so they settled on releasing both as a double A-side on 13 November 1989. It became their first UK top ten single, peaking at number eight.
cards.context: The single became their first UK top ten, peaking at number eight.

cards.headline: Mani's bassline was 'pinched' from a Young MC track
cards.snippet: In 1989, the Stone Roses' bassist Mani went clubbing "looking for things to pinch" and heard Kevin O'Neal's bassline in Young MC's "Know How". He adapted it for "Fools Gold", which the band wrote over James Brown's "The Funky Drummer" beat. Drummer Reni had to learn that beat for the track, according to singer Ian Brown. The result was a dance-oriented song that showcased the band's rhythm section.
cards.context: Ian Brown said the song was written over James Brown's 'The Funky Drummer', and Reni had to learn the beat.
